neighbours.label: ', just' after a complete clause, at the point where a comparison ('like ...' / 'as ...') is about to follow; adverbial 'just' (had just arrived) is silent
fire: The new stadium has a sliding roof, just like the one in Cardiff.
Prices here are set by the council, just like in the neighbouring towns.
The puppy chews everything in sight, just like her mother did.
Enemies respawn at random, just as they do in the earlier levels.
The bakery sells out by noon, just like every other Saturday.
This engine uses a timing chain, just like the rest of the range.
The app stores notes offline, just as its rival does.
Their second album was recorded live, just like the first.
quiet: The new stadium has a sliding roof, and it opened in Cardiff last May.
Prices here are set by the council, which meets in the town hall.
The puppy had just chewed everything in sight when we got home.
Enemies respawn at random, so the earlier levels stay hard.
The bakery had only just sold out when we arrived at noon.
This engine uses a timing chain, not a belt.
The app stores notes offline, but its rival does not.
Their second album was just recorded live in one evening.

notes: The pole's output promotes ' like' in many languages; card peaks are ',' and ' just' right before 'like'. Probes: ', just like/as' 0.18-0.36, ', much like' 0.18, 'X, like many others,' only 0.04-0.10, 'had just arrived' 0.00. Fractions are low because the corpus max (462) is an outlier.
